_readme: These are PLACEHOLDER calibration anchors used only if generate_synthetic_data.py cannot find real Tier 1 files in tier1_raw/. They are rough, order-of-magnitude estimates, NOT measured from real data. Once Tier 1 files are present, the script recomputes 'avg_order_value_local', 'delivery_days_mean', and 'delivery_days_std' directly from Olist/UCI and those override everything below. Document in DATA_DICTIONARY.md which values were placeholder-derived vs. calibrated-from-real-data, and on what date the recalibration happened.

US.source_note: PLACEHOLDER: general US e-commerce industry benchmarks, not measured. Refund rate loosely anchored to typical US e-commerce return-rate ranges.

DE.source_note: PLACEHOLDER. Germany has notably high e-commerce return rates versus other EU markets; 9% is a conservative placeholder pending real calibration.

GH.source_note: PLACEHOLDER: GHS 280 approximates a mid-range online order (roughly USD 18-22 at typical 2024-2026 GHS/USD rates). Longer delivery mean/std reflects generally less mature last-mile logistics infrastructure versus US/DE -- this is an assumption, not a measured fact, and should be called out explicitly as such in the README's limitations section.
